subject: phone in car
title: What If You Always Left Your Phone in the Car?

scenes.text: What if you always left your phone in the car? A mild 73-degree day is enough.
On a 73-degree day, the cabin can pass 100 degrees Fahrenheit within 25 minutes. A cracked window barely helps.
After an hour, it averages about 40 degrees hotter than outside. Dark dashboards can pass 180 degrees.
Your phone is meant to run only up to 95 degrees. Now it dims, slows down and stops charging.
Kept full at 104 degrees for a year, a lithium battery can keep only about 65 percent of its capacity.
The screen recovers once it cools. The battery doesn't. Apple says heat can permanently shorten its life.

description:
What if you always left your phone in the car? A Stanford study found parked cars heat up by about 40°F within an hour, even on mild days, and the National Weather Service notes 100°F within 25 minutes at 73°F outside.
Apple rates iPhones for 32-95°F and warns heat can permanently shorten battery life; Battery University estimates a full lithium battery stored at 40°C keeps about 65% capacity after a year.
